inputs.base_revenue_note: Calendar 2025 (Jan-Dec 2025) net sales, rebuilt as FY2025 (12m to 31-Jul-2025) 30,762 + five-month transition period (Aug-Dec 2025) 12,833 - same five months of 2024 12,279 (10-KT MD&A, FERG.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:1767). CY2026 guidance is framed off this calendar-2025 base, so Y1 = CY2026. The FY2026-5mo stub is NOT treated as a year anywhere in this model.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for the quarter ended 31-Mar-2026 (Q1 CY2026 presentation, adjusted EPS reconciliation). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. Period-end count after $236m of Q1 buybacks is ~1m lower; the weighted figure is the conservative choice.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition at 31-Mar-2026 (Q1 CY2026 presentation appendix): long-term debt 3,979 + short-term debt 148 + derivative liabilities 2 - cash 820 = 3,309. Lease liabilities (~$1.9bn) deliberately EXCLUDED: under US GAAP (ASC 842) operating lease cost is already inside SG&A/EBITDA and inside operating cash flow, so the lease is charged once, in the flows. Net debt / rolling-12m adjusted EBITDA 1.0x.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back, FY2025 (12m to 31-Jul-2025) = $28m (FERG.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:2543, comparative column). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed (it sits inside 'Other financing activities'), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc. FY2025's $28m is abnormally low (FY2021-24: 77/57/51/49; five-month stub Aug-Dec 2025: 70, reflecting the autumn grant cycle); the forward charge uses a ~$78m run-rate = 0.25% of revenue, not the FY2025 print.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: reported_fcf is the company's levered FCF (operating cash flow 1,908 - capex 305) for FY2025, the last audited twelve-month period; the five-month stub (OCF 859, capex 185, FCF 674) is seasonally flattered by a $553m receivables unwind and is excluded rather than annualised. last_fcf = 1,603 - 28 - 0 = 1,575. The projection does not start from this number: the engine builds unlevered owner FCF from components off CY2025 revenue (see assumptions), which is why year-1 modelled FCF (~$1.7bn after charging bolt-on M&A as capex) exceeds the levered reported figure.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of treasury shares $948m (cash flow statement); five-month stub $407m; Q1 CY2026 $236m. Ferguson is a consistent repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a convention. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are USD. The Yahoo chart endpoint returns 'No data found, symbol may be delisted' for FERG.L on the valuation date (1d, 5d and 1y ranges), and Yahoo search lists only the NYSE line (FERG) and German lines; the Feb-2026 10-KT still describes the company as listed on NYSE and LSE. current_price is therefore the NYSE regular close in USD and quote_currency is USD. GBp memo only: NYSE USD price x 100 / GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09) gives the equivalent pence value; no live LSE print was available to parity-check it. refresh_price.py should source the price from FERG, not FERG.L.
inputs.fiscal_year_note: Fiscal year end changed from 31 July to 31 December effective 1-Jan-2026; the Aug-Dec 2025 five-month transition period was reported on a Form 10-KT (stored as FY2026-5mo in the Metrics CSV).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + ~5% ERP x beta ~1.15 gives a cost of equity ~10%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.1% (5.5% pre-tax, 26% tax); ~7% debt weight at a ~$43bn market cap and $3.3bn net debt gives ~9.5%, rounded down to 9.0% for a BBB+ large-cap with 1.0x leverage and two-thirds RMI revenue. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows (adaptations 7f), not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost ($484m FY2025, $219m in the five-month stub) is expensed inside SG&A, so it is already inside adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow. Leases are therefore charged ONCE in the flows (treatment B by accounting standard); lease liabilities are excluded from net debt and lease_cost_pct_path is 0. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no non-controlling interests of substance.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials/distribution'), with owner-fcf-adaptations.md read for leases, working-capital sign, and charge-risk-once. Ferguson is North America's largest plumbing/HVAC/waterworks distributor; value is a stream of free cash flow, so the default engine applies. Key modelling choices: (1) base revenue is calendar 2025, not the July fiscal year and not the 5-month stub; (2) ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC EBITDA (the company's adjusted EBITDA is after SBC; CY2025 adjusted EBITDA 3,243 = 10.36% of sales, +0.25% SBC = ~10.6%), and adjusted EBITDA sits ~0.78pp above adjusted operating margin (CY2025 adj. operating profit 3,012 = 9.62%); (3) bolt-on M&A is treated as growth capex: the revenue paths include the ~1pp/yr that acquisitions have historically added, so capex_pct_path = ~1.2% PP&E/technology capex (CY2026 guidance $350-400m) + ~1.0% acquisitions (FY2020-25 average $397m/yr); (4) working capital is a cash CONSUMER for a distributor (inventory + receivables > payables, NWC ~12-13% of sales), so wc_capture_pct is negative; (5) cash tax 26% in every year = CY2026 guided adjusted ETR, and the 21.6% five-month rate (uncertain-tax-position release) is not perpetuated; (6) interest income is not stripped because the company is a net borrower; (7) terminal cap 15x owner FCF for a cyclical distributor (method section 4), which binds in base and bull.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: CY2026 guidance (low-to-mid single digit) anchored to the 3yr revenue CAGR (2.5%, FY2022-FY2025, post-inflation) plus ~1pp/yr from bolt-on acquisitions; the 10-year base path averages ~4%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.9% vs revenue 9.1% and EPS 17.1% (>30% divergence). Not a signal: book equity is held down by ~$5.6bn of buybacks and ~$3.9bn of dividends over FY2020-25, so equity CAGR is not the growth anchor for a repurchaser. The 5yr revenue CAGR is inflated by 2021-22 commodity inflation (FY2022 +25%); the 3yr figure is the cleaner read.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2020-FY2025 (July year-ends) only; the FY2026-5mo transition stub is excluded from every CAGR. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income nil): FY2020 1,233; FY2021 1,064; FY2022 802; FY2023 2,231; FY2024 1,452; FY2025 1,575. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR of 25% is a working-capital artefact (FY2022 inventory build, FY2023 destock) and should not be read as trend. Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are nearly identical because SBC is ~0.2% of revenue.

base.growth_rationale: CY2026 3.5% = midpoint of 'low-to-mid single digit' guidance and Q1 CY2026's +3.6%. 2027-29 4.5-5.0% assumes a modest residential recovery as mortgage rates ease, continued non-residential/large-project strength and ~1pp/yr of bolt-ons; fades to 2.5% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 10.6% in CY2026 = CY2026 guided adjusted operating margin midpoint 9.6% + ~0.8pp depreciation/non-acquired amortisation + 0.25pp SBC. Drifts to 11.0% (adjusted operating margin ~10.0%) by 2030 on HVAC/waterworks mix and scale, slightly below the FY2022 inflation-peak 10.4% adjusted operating margin.
base.capex_rationale: 1.2% PP&E/technology capex (CY2026 guidance $350-400m) + 1.0% bolt-on acquisitions (FY2020-25 average $397m/yr, 1.4% of sales, over a period of faster growth).
base.wc_rationale: Distributor: NWC ~12-13% of sales, so each $1 of revenue growth absorbs ~$0.12 of cash. FY2025 actual drag was -$316m on +$1,127m of sales (-28%), an inventory/receivables-heavy year; -12% is the structural rate.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of guidance in CY2026, then a genuine housing recovery (starts and RMI) in 2027-28 layered on an extended data-center/semiconductor/onshoring cycle and a faster M&A cadence (the $2bn new buyback authorisation funded alongside, not instead of, deals).
bull.margin_rationale: Adjusted operating margin reaches ~10.6% (pre-SBC EBITDA 11.6%), modestly above the FY2022 peak, as HVAC dual-trade conversions, own-brand mix and DC network leverage compound.

bear.growth_rationale: Residential (half of sales) falls further through 2027 as housing starts drop the 6-17% industry trackers forecast, while the data-center build-out peaks and stops offsetting it; price deflation in copper/PVC adds to the volume decline. Recovers only to market growth from 2029; M&A slows (capex 2.0%).
bear.margin_rationale: Tariff cost pass-through fails in a soft-demand market and operating deleverage takes adjusted operating margin back to ~8.8% (pre-SBC EBITDA 9.8%), near the FY2020-21 trough levels.

scenario_narratives.base: Ferguson keeps taking share in a fragmented ~$340bn market while its two end markets move in opposite directions: residential (~50% of sales) stays flat-to-down through 2026 and recovers gradually from 2027 as rates ease, while non-residential (waterworks, commercial/mechanical, data-center and fab projects) grows mid-to-high single digits. CY2026 lands inside guidance (sales +3.5%, adjusted operating margin ~9.6%, capex $350-400m, 26% tax), medium-term growth runs ~4-5% including ~1pp of bolt-ons, and margin drifts toward 10% adjusted operating / 11% pre-SBC EBITDA as the HVAC-everywhere and distribution-centre investments mature. Net debt stays ~1x EBITDA; buybacks keep the share count flat. Terminal value is bound by the 15x owner-FCF cap, not Gordon growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: The housing cycle turns in 2027: starts and RMI recover as mortgage rates fall, just as the large-capital-project pipeline (data centres, semiconductors, biotech, onshoring; ~$50bn addressable through 2030) continues to build. Ferguson converts both into 6-7% growth for three years with M&A adding on top, and scale economics plus mix push adjusted operating margin through the FY2022 peak to ~10.6%. The bull case needs residential recovery AND continued non-residential strength AND margin expansion to coincide, which is why its weight is held below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: Residential weakens further through 2027 (industry trackers already forecast 2026 starts down 6-17%), the data-center build-out proves closer to a peak than a ramp, and commodity deflation returns, so revenue stalls for two years. Tariff costs (~50% on many steel/aluminium/copper products) cannot be fully passed through into a soft market and operating deleverage takes adjusted operating margin back toward FY2020-21 levels (~8.8%). Growth resumes only at market rate from 2029 with a slower M&A cadence. The balance sheet (1.0x leverage, $2.4bn undrawn facilities) is not at risk in this path; it is an earnings-power bear case, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull down to 25%: it needs three independent things (housing recovery, continued data-center capex, margin expansion past the FY2022 peak) to arrive together. Bear up to 25%: the near-term residential and tariff headwinds are live and documented in industry forecasts, not hypothetical, though the balance sheet makes it a cyclical bear rather than a distress one. Base 50%: CY2026 guidance was reaffirmed in May 2026 and Q1 tracked it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis: unlevered owner FCF with SBC fully expensed (immaterial here at ~0.25% of sales, so house and street values nearly coincide), bolt-on M&A charged as growth capex because the growth path includes what it buys, working capital charged as a cash consumer, leases charged once via US GAAP operating cost, and a 15x cyclical cap on terminal FCF. Ferguson is a high-quality compounder of a thin-margin distribution model; the valuation question is price, not quality. At the current price the market is paying roughly 27x levered owner FCF (~21x CY2026 adjusted EPS), which this model only reaches on the bull path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Residential construction/RMI stays depressed longer than the base path's 2027 recovery (half of revenue)
Data-center/large-project cycle peaks, removing the non-residential offset that has carried growth since FY2024
Tariff and commodity (copper, steel, PVC) swings: deflation squeezes gross margin, inflation that cannot be passed through squeezes it too
M&A treated as recurring capex at 1% of sales: if bolt-ons stop, growth should be read ~1pp lower, roughly offsetting the saved cash
Working-capital capture at -12% of incremental revenue; a single destock/restock year moves FCF by several hundred million dollars either way
Terminal value is cap-bound at 15x owner FCF; a buyer paying 18-20x for a scaled distributor (as the market does today) adds ~$30-40/share
